chapter: Noble Sissle, Manhattan School and Philadelphia memories
title: Broadway show music and club dates compared with jazz
summary: Show playing is rigid compared to jazz; club dates are dance sets.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How about the music itself, to go from playing jazz, where you had a chance to improvise?
In the Diamond Horseshoe, we were playing all Broadway show music and things like that.

Yeah, that’s what they played, basically. So that – without – until I’m just mentioning it, I didn’t even realize – without realizing it, I was being prepared for this thing, because the music I was playing at the Diamond Horseshoe was all basically Broadway show music.
So this was a chance. Then you went into a show. What I heard from other musicians is that it’s kind of a shock after you play jazz, because you’re . . . .

Oh, it’s just different. It’s so rigid, yeah, very rigid, and by comparison, you might say it’s kind of corny. It isn’t really corny. It’s just a completely different style of music. It’s like doing club dates, where you go out and play these club dates. It’s an entirely different thing.
A club date is like a party or a dance or something?
Yeah. It’s like a dance. You play one thing after the other. You segue from one tune into the other, and different tempos, for the benefit of the dancers.
